site.title: Theodore Roosevelt Presidential Library Quizzes
site.tagline: Preview a quiz, copy the snippet, paste it into any page on trlibrary.com.

_note: Placement is manual: paste the snippet for a given quiz id onto the page it belongs to. `placement` records the intended page for reference only - nothing reads it. `draft: true` means the quiz file does not exist yet.

quizzes.title: T.R. in the Badlands
quizzes.blurb: In 1883 a bespectacled New York assemblyman got off a train in Dakota Territory to hunt buffalo. He left three years later a cattleman. Fifteen questions on the country that made him.
quizzes.imageAlt: Theodore Roosevelt in buckskin, photographed in 1885

quizzes.title: The Making of a Boy
quizzes.blurb: Asthma nearly killed him. A bedroom museum, a taxidermy tutor, and a father who told him to make his body. Fifteen questions on the years before anyone had heard of him.
quizzes.imageAlt: Theodore Roosevelt as a small boy, about two years old

quizzes.title: The Youngest Man in the Assembly
quizzes.blurb: Elected at twenty-three, dismissed as a dude, and fighting the machine within a year. Fifteen questions on Roosevelt's first taste of power.
quizzes.imageAlt: A composite portrait of the members of the New York State Assembly, 1882-1884, made up of separate head-and-shoulders photographs

quizzes.title: Fifteen Years to the White House
quizzes.blurb: Civil service reformer, police commissioner, governor, vice president — and then Buffalo. Fifteen questions on the climb.
quizzes.imageAlt: Theodore Roosevelt as Assistant Secretary of the Navy

quizzes.title: The Rough Riders
quizzes.blurb: Cowboys, Ivy League athletes and lawmen, mustered into one regiment in a matter of weeks. Fifteen questions on 1898.
quizzes.imageAlt: Roosevelt and the Rough Riders on the captured hill

quizzes.title: The Square Deal
quizzes.blurb: Forty-two years old and suddenly president. Trusts, coal strikes, a canal, and a Nobel Prize. Fifteen questions on eight years.
quizzes.imageAlt: Theodore Roosevelt in his private office

quizzes.title: Two Hundred and Thirty Million Acres
quizzes.blurb: Parks, forests, monuments, bird reserves — the legacy that outlasted everything else he did. Fifteen questions on what he saved.
quizzes.imageAlt: Theodore Roosevelt and John Muir on Glacier Point, Yosemite

quizzes.title: After the White House
quizzes.blurb: An African safari, a third-party crusade, a bullet in the chest, and an unmapped river in the Amazon. Fifteen questions on his last decade.
quizzes.imageAlt: Roosevelt and Carl Akeley on the African expedition

quizzes.title: The People Around Him
quizzes.blurb: Edith, John Muir, Booker T. Washington, and the rivals who sharpened him. Fifteen questions on the company he kept.
quizzes.imageAlt: Théobald Chartran's painted portrait of Edith Kermit Roosevelt in a plumed hat, seated on a stone bench in a garden

quizzes.title: Life at Sagamore Hill
quizzes.blurb: Six children, a pony in the White House lift, and a sandbank the whole household raced down. Fifteen questions on the Roosevelts at home.
quizzes.imageAlt: Theodore and Edith Roosevelt seated with five children in a studio group portrait, the youngest a baby

quizzes.title: The Strenuous Life
quizzes.blurb: Boxing, judo, point-to-point walks through anything in the way. Fifteen questions on a creed he practised before he preached it.
quizzes.imageAlt: Theodore Roosevelt mounted in ranch clothes

quizzes.title: The Naturalist
quizzes.blurb: The president who kept lists, argued with ornithologists and never stopped observing. Eleven questions on Roosevelt and the natural world.
quizzes.imageAlt: Roosevelt reading in front of his tent in camp

quizzes.title: Where History Happened
quizzes.blurb: A Manhattan townhouse, a Badlands cabin, a hill above Oyster Bay, and the White House he renamed. Fifteen questions on the places that kept him.
quizzes.imageAlt: Roosevelt's birthplace at 28 East 20th Street

quizzes.title: The Author President
quizzes.blurb: Some thirty-five books and thousands of articles, most of them written after living the story first. Fifteen questions on Roosevelt in print.
quizzes.imageAlt: The library at Sagamore Hill

quizzes.title: Fact or Fiction
quizzes.blurb: He hated being called Teddy, and that is the least of it. Fifteen questions separating the famous stories from the record.
quizzes.imageAlt: Berryman's 1902 cartoon that started the teddy bear

quizzes.title: The Measure of the Man
quizzes.blurb: Mount Rushmore, presidential rankings, and a name on a national park. Fifteen questions on how America decided to remember him.
quizzes.imageAlt: The Fraser equestrian statue at the Roosevelt Memorial

quizzes.title: The Teddy Bear
quizzes.blurb: A president refused a shot he thought unsporting, a cartoonist drew it, and a Brooklyn shopkeeper wrote for permission to use the name. Twelve questions on how a Mississippi hunt made the world's most successful toy.
quizzes.imageAlt: Berryman's 1902 cartoon "Drawing the line in Mississippi"

quizzes.title: The White House Menagerie
quizzes.blurb: A badger named after the boy who caught it, a snake named after a thin aunt, and a pony that took the passenger lift. Twelve questions on the Roosevelt animals.
quizzes.imageAlt: Archie Roosevelt with Josiah, his pet badger

quizzes.title: The Twenty-Seventh of October
quizzes.blurb: Born on 27 October 1858 and married on the same date twenty-two years later. One birthday he spent walking the grounds with a bullet in his chest. Ten questions for the day itself.
quizzes.imageAlt: Theodore Roosevelt as a small boy, about two years old

quizzes.title: Christmas at the Roosevelts'
quizzes.blurb: The president who protected 230 million acres had reservations about cutting an evergreen. His nine-year-old son smuggled one into a closet anyway. Ten questions on Christmas in the Roosevelt house - including the last one.
quizzes.imageAlt: President Roosevelt seated between his sons Archie and Quentin, 1904

quizzes.title: Eight Thousand Handshakes
quizzes.blurb: Every New Year's Day the White House opened its doors and anyone willing to queue could shake the president's hand. On 1 January 1907 an awful lot of people did. Ten questions on the most exhausting tradition in American public life.
quizzes.imageAlt: Members of the public filing in to the White House for the New Year's reception

quizzes.title: The Dickinson Oration
quizzes.blurb: In 1886 a twenty-seven-year-old New York ranchman rode a freight train thirty-five miles to give a Fourth of July speech in a Dakota town six years old. One listener told him afterwards he would be president. Eleven questions on the best Independence Day in North Dakota history.
quizzes.imageAlt: Dickinson, Dakota Territory, in 1883

quizzes.title: The Roosevelts at War
quizzes.blurb: Four sons in France and Mesopotamia, a father refused the division he begged for, and a telegram that never came. Thirteen questions on the Roosevelts and the First World War.
quizzes.imageAlt: Quentin Roosevelt with his Nieuport aircraft

quizzes.title: Greatheart
quizzes.blurb: The nights his father drove him through the streets to force air into his lungs, the substitute he hired in 1861, and the verdict his son never revised. Fourteen questions on Theodore Roosevelt Senior.
quizzes.imageAlt: Portrait of Theodore Roosevelt Sr. hanging at Sagamore Hill, photographed in 1966

quizzes.title: The Path Between the Seas
quizzes.blurb: A French failure, a revolution that lasted a day, a doctor who fought mosquitoes, and the biggest earth-moving job ever attempted. Fifteen questions on the canal.
quizzes.imageAlt: A Bucyrus steam shovel working the Culebra Cut

quizzes.title: The River of Doubt
quizzes.blurb: An unmapped Amazon tributary, a Brazilian co-commander, a drowning, a murder, and an infected leg a thousand miles from help. Fifteen questions on the expedition that nearly killed him.
quizzes.imageAlt: Roosevelt and Candido Rondon on the Brazilian expedition

quizzes.title: Sixteen Battleships
quizzes.blurb: He had money to send them halfway and dared Congress to leave them there. Fourteen questions on the cruise that took the American navy round the world.
quizzes.imageAlt: The battle fleet leaving Hampton Roads

quizzes.title: The Body He Made
quizzes.blurb: Asthma, a warning about his heart, a blind eye nobody knew about, a bullet that stayed in, and fevers that came back until the end. Thirteen questions on sixty years of hard use.
quizzes.imageAlt: The 1912 X-ray plate showing the bullet in Roosevelt's chest

quizzes.title: The Peacemaker
quizzes.blurb: Two empires at war, a navy yard in Maine, a buffet lunch that solved an unsolvable protocol problem, and the first Nobel Prize ever won by an American. Fourteen questions.
quizzes.imageAlt: The Russian and Japanese envoys with Roosevelt aboard the Mayflower

quizzes.title: Emperor of the Bad Lands
quizzes.blurb: A French aristocrat pitched a tent on the Little Missouri in 1883, named a town for his wife, and set out to slaughter beef on the range and ship it east. Fourteen questions on the Marquis de Mores.
quizzes.imageAlt: The de Mores abattoir at Medora

quizzes.title: The Winter That Ended the Open Range
quizzes.blurb: The grass was eaten bare, the range was overstocked, and Roosevelt had said so in print. Then it began to snow. Fifteen questions on the winter of 1886-87.
quizzes.imageAlt: Cattle drifted against a wire fence in a blizzard

quizzes.title: Seventy Thousand Acres
quizzes.blurb: The only national park named for a person, in the country that made him. Fifteen questions on how it came to exist and what is actually there.
quizzes.imageAlt: The North Dakota Badlands

quizzes.title: What Lives Out There
quizzes.blurb: The bison he came to hunt were already gone. Fifteen questions on the animals of the North Dakota Badlands, what Roosevelt saw, and what a visitor is likely to see now.
quizzes.imageAlt: Deer wading the shallows of the upper Heart River, North Dakota, 1905

quizzes.title: Four Men and a Bullet
quizzes.blurb: He won most of the primaries and lost the nomination, so he started his own party. Then someone shot him and he finished the speech. Fifteen questions on the strangest election in American history.
quizzes.imageAlt: Cartoon: We are against his politics, but we like his grit

quizzes.title: No Coal and Winter Coming
quizzes.blurb: A hundred and forty thousand men walked out of the anthracite mines in May 1902, and the operators would not talk to them. Fourteen questions on the strike that changed what a president could do.
quizzes.imageAlt: Breaker boys at the Woodward Coal Mines, Kingston, Pennsylvania

quizzes.title: Thanksgiving with the Roosevelts
quizzes.blurb: He ranked it a distant second to Christmas, which did not stop the day from carrying a good deal of his life: a vow made at twenty in a house outside Boston, his father’s standing appointment with the newsboys, a possum, a turkey and a newspaper war. Twelve questions on the fourth Thursday in November.
quizzes.imageAlt: The White House State Dining Room with mounted game heads on the panelled walls

quizzes.title: Inauguration Day, 1905
quizzes.blurb: He had taken the oath once already, in a borrowed suit in a friend’s parlour in Buffalo. This one was his: a Lincoln relic on his finger, Rough Riders at his elbow, and thirty-five thousand people coming up Pennsylvania Avenue, six Native leaders on horseback among them. Twelve questions on Roosevelt’s only inauguration.
quizzes.imageAlt: The east front of the Capitol on 4 March 1905, flags hung between the columns and a dense crowd on the steps

quizzes.title: Election Night, 1904
quizzes.blurb: On 8 November 1904 Roosevelt won the presidency in his own right by the biggest popular margin anyone had managed. Then, warning nobody, he told the reporters he would never accept another nomination — a sentence he spent the rest of his career wishing back. Thirteen questions on one night at the White House.
quizzes.imageAlt: Colour cartoon of a giant Theodore Roosevelt leaning over the roof of the White House with the Capitol behind

quizzes.title: The Sixth of January
quizzes.blurb: He died in his sleep at Sagamore Hill in the early morning of 6 January 1919, six months after his youngest son was killed in France. Fourteen questions on his last year, the day itself, and what the country did when it heard.
quizzes.imageAlt: Mounted police leading the funeral cortege at Oyster Bay, January 1919

quizzes.title: The Fourteenth of February
quizzes.blurb: His mother and his wife died in the same house on West 57th Street on 14 February 1884, eleven hours apart, two days after his daughter was born. Twelve questions on the day, the people in the house, and what he did afterwards.
quizzes.imageAlt: Alice Hathaway Lee Roosevelt, about 1883

quizzes.title: Mittie, Bamie and Edith
quizzes.blurb: A Georgia girl who never accepted the outcome of the war, a sister who lent her brother a house to be president in, and a wife who put him on a daily allowance. Thirteen questions on the women who made Theodore Roosevelt.
quizzes.imageAlt: The Roosevelt family and friends photographed on the Nile, 1872-73

quizzes.title: After the Charge
quizzes.blurb: The regiment lasted four months. The men who filled it lasted another seventy-seven years, and Roosevelt's own sons carried it forward into two more wars. Fourteen questions for Veterans Day on what happened after the fighting stopped.
quizzes.imageAlt: Officers of the Rough Riders at the camp at Montauk Point, 1898

quizzes.title: Five Ways to Save a Place
quizzes.blurb: The famous number is 230 million acres, and the number tells you nothing. Roosevelt had five separate legal tools and used every one differently - on a five-acre rookery in Florida, on eight hundred thousand acres of Arizona canyon, on a hill in North Dakota. Fourteen questions on the specifics.
quizzes.imageAlt: The governors of every state and territory on the White House portico, May 1908

quizzes.title: The Twenty-Sixth
quizzes.blurb: Born under Buchanan, employed by three presidents before he was one, sworn in beside a friend's bookshelves in Buffalo, and carved into a mountain in South Dakota. Thirteen questions on where Roosevelt sits in the line.
quizzes.imageAlt: The library of the Wilcox house in Buffalo where Roosevelt took the oath

quizzes.title: The President Who Birded
quizzes.blurb: He shot his first bird on the Nile at fourteen, published a bird list before he could vote, and named a fox sparrow from a scrap of down on a White House path. Thirteen questions for the spring migration.
quizzes.imageAlt: Chromolithograph of chestnut-sided and yellow warblers on a birch branch

quizzes.title: A Very Irregular Education
quizzes.blurb: He never sat in a classroom until he was seventeen, was hopeless at Latin and unbeatable at natural history, and walked out of law school after a year. Thirteen questions for the start of term.
quizzes.imageAlt: Holworthy Hall in Harvard Yard, photographed in the nineteenth century

quizzes.title: Two Weddings
quizzes.blurb: The first was at noon on his own birthday, in New England sunshine, with his brother holding the ring. The second was in a London fog so thick nobody could see the altar. Fourteen questions on Theodore Roosevelt's two marriages.
quizzes.imageAlt: Portrait of Alice Hathaway Lee as a young woman

quizzes.title: The Country Before Roosevelt
quizzes.blurb: The Mandan had a story about who made this country. The Lakota wintered on the upper river, French trappers cursed it in their own language, the Army built a post beside the crossing and the railroad renamed it Pyramid Park for the tourist trade. Fourteen questions on the Badlands before Theodore Roosevelt ever saw them.
quizzes.imageAlt: Eroded badlands ridges and bare clay hillocks falling away toward a distant valley

quizzes.title: How the Open Range Worked
quizzes.blurb: No fences, no deeds, no sheriff worth the name — and somehow tens of thousands of cattle grazed the same country and got sorted out again every spring. Fourteen questions on the round-up, the brand book, the line camps, what a cowboy was paid, and the stockmen's association Roosevelt chaired at twenty-six.
quizzes.imageAlt: Cowhands holding a band of saddle horses inside a rope stretched from a wagon

quizzes.title: The Spine of the Badlands
quizzes.blurb: Shallow enough to walk across in August, and it carved a hundred miles of canyon country doing it. Thirteen questions on the Little Missouri River — where it rises, which way it runs, the town called Little Misery on its west bank, and what became of the mouth.
quizzes.imageAlt: A wide bend of the Little Missouri with a low cut bank and cottonwoods on the far shore

quizzes.title: How the Badlands Were Made
quizzes.blurb: A swamp full of crocodiles, coal seams that catch fire and bake the clay above them into brick, petrified stumps still standing where the trees grew, and a river shoved off course by a wall of ice. Fifteen questions on Badlands geology.
quizzes.imageAlt: Badlands buttes near Medora with pale layered clay slopes and a band of red rock along the ridge

quizzes.title: Twins, and Nobody Knows Which Was Born First
quizzes.blurb: A territory that once reached into Montana, a capital carried off by a railroad before dawn, a division fight that ran for a decade, and a signing arranged so neither Dakota could claim to be older. Fourteen questions on North Dakota statehood.
quizzes.imageAlt: An 1883 bird's-eye lithograph of Bismarck, Dakota Territory, with steamboats on the Missouri

quizzes.title: Medora Now
quizzes.blurb: A town of a hundred and twenty-one people, a national park in three pieces, a French nobleman's house on its bluff, a musical under the stars, and a presidential library with a prairie growing on the roof. Thirteen questions on what is there now.
quizzes.imageAlt: The Little Missouri River winding through banded badlands ridges seen from a high overlook

quizzes.title: The Gilded Age
quizzes.blurb: A novelist named the era, and he did not mean it kindly. Fourteen questions on the fortunes, the trusts, the tenements and the crash — and on an argument about inequality that historians have still not finished having.
quizzes.imageAlt: Colour cartoon of enormous money bags labelled with the names of trusts looming over the seated United States Senate

quizzes.title: The Progressive Era
quizzes.blurb: For twenty years Americans of every stripe agreed something had to be done, then argued about what. Fourteen questions on city commissions, primary ballots, factory inspectors — and the reforms that split the reformers.
quizzes.imageAlt: A vast crowd filling a wide avenue, with a banner reading We Demand an Amendment to the Constitution

quizzes.title: The Muckrakers
quizzes.blurb: For a decade the biggest thing in American publishing was the investigative exposé, sold for a dime. The word was coined by a president who meant it as an insult. Fourteen questions on Tarbell, Steffens, Sinclair and Riis.
quizzes.imageAlt: Colour cartoon of journalists drawn as medieval knights on horseback, their shields and banners lettered with magazine titles

quizzes.title: The Frontier That Closed
quizzes.blurb: In 1890 the Census Bureau said it could no longer draw a line between settled and unsettled America, and three years later a young historian built a theory of the national character on it. Fifteen questions on homesteads, cattle, railroads and the nations already there.
quizzes.imageAlt: A homesteading family standing in front of a low sod house on the Nebraska plains, with a cow grazing on the roof

quizzes.title: Coming to America, 1880-1920
quizzes.blurb: Twenty-five million people arrived in forty years, and a great many meant to go home again. Fifteen questions on the ships, the stations, the tenements, the laws, and the arguments Americans had about all of it.
quizzes.imageAlt: Wood engraving of steerage passengers crowding the deck of an ocean steamer as it passes the Statue of Liberty

quizzes.title: The Women Who Ran the Era
quizzes.blurb: A reporter had herself committed to an asylum. A settlement-house founder followed the garbage wagons at dawn. A teacher sued a railroad and would not march at the back. Fourteen questions on the women of Roosevelt's America - and not the ones at Sagamore Hill.
quizzes.imageAlt: An enormous crowd filling Pennsylvania Avenue in Washington, the Capitol dome visible in the distance

quizzes.title: The War of 1898
quizzes.blurb: Cubans had been fighting Spain for thirty years before an American battleship blew up in Havana harbour. Fifteen questions on what set the war off, what the inquiries actually found, and what killed most of the Americans who died.
quizzes.imageAlt: The wreck of the battleship Maine in Havana harbour, only a mast and torn plating above the water

quizzes.title: A World Power
quizzes.blurb: In eighteen months the United States acquired Hawaii, Puerto Rico, Guam and the Philippines, and began arguing about whether a republic could hold colonies and stay one. Fifteen questions on the empire debate, the Open Door and the Roosevelt Corollary.
quizzes.imageAlt: The president reading his annual message to the cabinet before sending it to Congress, 1903

quizzes.title: The Other Roosevelts
quizzes.blurb: Two presidents, two branches, one wedding that joined them, and twenty years later the halves of the family campaigning against each other. Fourteen questions on Oyster Bay and Hyde Park.
quizzes.imageAlt: A tintype of four young Roosevelts and Edith Carow outdoors at Oyster Bay in 1875

quizzes.title: Trust-Busting
quizzes.blurb: A trust started life as a piece of legal furniture and ended as the word Americans used for everything they feared about big business. Fifteen questions on the device, the statute nobody used, Northern Securities, the Bureau of Corporations, and the rule of reason.
quizzes.imageAlt: A 1902 newspaper cartoon of a swaggering bully labelled Standard Oil Trust with a sleepy policeman behind him

quizzes.title: Roosevelt and the Press
quizzes.blurb: He gave reporters a room in the White House, a shave to watch and a great deal of news, and cut them off when they broke the terms. Fourteen questions on the bargain, the Ananias Club, and the Michigan libel trial that ended in a verdict of six cents.
quizzes.imageAlt: Theodore Roosevelt in a hat and spectacles talking to two men, one writing on a folded sheet of paper

quizzes.title: Roosevelt and the Camera
quizzes.blurb: Some of the most famous pictures of him were staged after the fact, a hit film about his safari was shot in Chicago with an actor, and the man doing the real photographic work was his son. Thirteen questions on how the images were made.
quizzes.imageAlt: Theodore Roosevelt in fringed buckskin with a rifle, seated before a painted studio backdrop in 1885

quizzes.title: A Book a Day
quizzes.blurb: He got through a book a day and often more, in several languages, and he did it in railway lavatories, in cow camps and on the floor of a national convention. Fourteen questions on the other Roosevelt library - the one he read rather than the one he wrote.
quizzes.imageAlt: The book-lined library at Sagamore Hill, with a portrait over the mantel and a zebra skin on the floor

quizzes.title: The Sagamore Table
quizzes.blurb: A coffee cup his son compared to a bathtub, a wife who ran the White House off a written list, a caterer paid out of the President's own pocket, and a pantry kept locked against the boys. Fourteen questions on what the Roosevelts ate and drank.
quizzes.imageAlt: Sagamore Hill seen from the lawn, a large shingled house with a wide porch behind a weeping tree

quizzes.title: The Objects He Carried
quizzes.blurb: A silver knife from Tiffany's, a buckskin suit sewn in a Dakota shack, an English double rifle subscribed for by fifty strangers, and the Winchester he rated above every other gun he owned. Fourteen questions on the objects, their makers, and what survives.
quizzes.imageAlt: Theodore Roosevelt seated in a fringed buckskin suit and fur cap, a knife at his belt and an engraved rifle across his knees

quizzes.title: The Dakota Papers
quizzes.blurb: A cattle contract in his own hand, a ledger everyone quotes for what he lost and nobody quotes twice, four hundred dollars for ground he never owned, and one famous sentence nobody has traced to him. Thirteen expert questions on how the Badlands story is known.
quizzes.imageAlt: A newspaper advertisement for two ranches, with four cattle engravings showing a maltese cross, a triangle and an elkhorn marked on their sides

quizzes.title: The Machinery of Conservation
quizzes.blurb: A forestry school in France, a bureau with no forests, one Iowa congressman who wrote two of the load-bearing statutes, a commission Congress killed by amendment, and a world conference that was invited, accepted and cancelled. Fourteen expert questions.
quizzes.imageAlt: Theodore Roosevelt in a top hat and Gifford Pinchot standing together on the deck of a river steamer, seen from behind

quizzes.title: The Instruments of Power
quizzes.blurb: An amendment slipped into an appropriations bill, an intermediary between a president and a senator who would not speak to him, a recess that lasted an instant, and a treaty the Senate refused. Fourteen expert questions on how the White House actually worked.
quizzes.imageAlt: A large desk with two lamps and stacked books in a panelled office, an empty cane-backed chair beside it

quizzes.title: The First Volunteer Cavalry
quizzes.blurb: The carbine Leonard Wood pulled strings to get, the stable fatigues the men wore because nothing else was in the depot, the transport Roosevelt took by running his regiment to the quay. Thirteen expert questions on 1898.
quizzes.imageAlt: Six officers of the First Volunteer Cavalry standing among pine trees at Tampa, Roosevelt at the right

quizzes.title: Did He Really Say That?
quizzes.blurb: Some of his best-loved lines are things he was quoting from somebody else, some are half a sentence with the other half cut off, and some he never said at all. Thirteen expert questions on misquoting T.R.
quizzes.imageAlt: Theodore Roosevelt bent over a desk in shirt cuffs, writing with a pen under a hanging lamp

quizzes.title: The Whole Life
quizzes.blurb: An uncle in Liverpool, a boxing match at Harvard, a bill about cigars, a post office in Baltimore, a submarine in Long Island Sound, and a French prime minister writing to an American president about him. Fifteen questions at maximum difficulty, birth to death.
quizzes.imageAlt: Theodore Roosevelt in his early thirties as a Civil Service Commissioner, seated in a dark suit

quizzes.title: The Making of a Boy: Family Edition
quizzes.blurb: Dead mice in the icebox, a snapping turtle tied to the laundry tub, and a boy of nine writing his own book about insects. Nine short questions on T.R.'s childhood, written for a family to play together.
quizzes.imageAlt: Theodore Roosevelt as a boy of about eleven, in a large bow tie

quizzes.title: What He Saved: Family Edition
quizzes.blurb: A cave with stone honeycomb on its walls, houses built into a cliff, and a forest of fallen trees that turned into rock. Nine short questions on the land Roosevelt protected, written for a family to play together.
quizzes.imageAlt: The stone entrance arch at the north gate of Yellowstone National Park

quizzes.title: The Rough Riders: Family Edition
quizzes.blurb: Twenty thousand men wrote in asking to join. They trained for two weeks, a boy from Tennessee stowed away on the ship, and they ate beans Roosevelt paid for himself. Nine short questions, written for a family to play together.
quizzes.imageAlt: Theodore Roosevelt in Rough Rider uniform, mounted on a horse
